svg.title: nuntio system architecture
svg.desc: The nuntio process: the main thread owns the window, the wgpu renderer, tabs and panes; one PTY reader thread per pane parses shell output into alacritty_terminal and wakes the main thread through UserEvents; service threads watch the config, sample the system, check for updates and read the clipboard. Child processes are shells in a PTY or ConPTY, WSL shells behind the nuntio-wsl relay, and the nuntio-config settings TUI, which writes the config file that nuntio hot-reloads.
svg.text: GPU terminal emulator for Linux, macOS and Windows · one window, tabs, split panes · Rust workspace on alacritty_terminal and wgpu
Terminal bytes — PTY, ConPTY, framed pipes to nuntio-wsl
UserEvent through the EventLoopProxy (thread → main thread)
Config files — atomic write, notify, hot reload
single window · only the main thread touches the window, the renderer, tabs and panes
winit event loop · ControlFlow::Wait · App = Core + WindowState · crates/nuntio/src/app.rs
keys → Bindings (first match wins) or input::encode_key → TermHandle::write · idle ≈ 0 % CPU
each sends UserEvent through a cloned EventLoopProxy
IoLoop over a Backend: Unix PTY · ConPTY · WslPipe (Windows) · ExitGuard closes the pane even on panic
one per pane · spawned by Core::spawn_pane
macOS wraps the shell in login(1)
also the fallback for WSL panes
raw PTY bytes · relay: one poll loop
build.rs cross-builds it for x86_64 musl
no IPC: hot reload is the live preview
on the PATH of nuntio's panes only
one JSON line per request and reply
ci.yml: fmt · clippy · tests on 3 OSes,
release.yml on v* tags → GitHub release
invalid file → banner, previous config stays
